plants.name: Prunus mume
plants.description: Gnarled branches still bare of leaves burst into fragrant, blossoms that look like tiny rosettes. They open while late-winter chill lingers, and they are often the first sign that spring is on its way. Their sweet, spicy perfume drifts through gardens and orchards.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (roughly late January to mid-March, depending on the variety and the elevation)
plants.location: Japan, including the Kantō and Kansai regions, and eastern China
plants.funFact: Ume blossoms have been celebrated in East Asian poetry and art for over a thousand years. In Japan, people saw them as the herald of spring long before cherry blossoms took that role.

plants.name: Narcissus pseudonarcissus
plants.description: Nodding golden trumpets framed by pale, swept-back petals light up woodland edges and meadows. Whole hillsides turn buttery yellow as the flowers sway in the cool breeze. A single drift of them can brighten a gray early-spring day.
plants.bloomingSeason: Late winter to early spring (typically February to April, with peak bloom often in March)
plants.location: Western and central Europe, especially the woodlands and meadows of England, Wales and France
plants.funFact: Daffodils contain a toxic alkaloid called lycorine, which is why deer and rabbits leave them alone. One compound from related Narcissus species, galantamine, is used in medicine.

plants.name: Colchicum autumnale
plants.description: This is a late-summer and autumn flower, so it is not in bloom on March 11 and should not be on this list.
plants.funFact: Its leaves appear in spring, while its flowers come in autumn.
